t: Check Knight Tour Configuration — Order Verification
o: grid[cell] tells the visit order of each square. The tour is valid iff step 0 is at the top-left and consecutive steps 0,1,...,n²−1 are legal knight moves apart. Rather than searching, we invert the grid: place each step number's coordinates in an array, then verify all n²−1 consecutive pairs. Example 1 passes all move checks; in Example 2 some consecutive pair differs by something other than (1,2)/(2,1), so false. With n ≤ 7 this is trivially fast — O(n²).
k: Invert the permutation: pos[t] = coordinates of the t-th visited cell.
Validity = pos[0] == (0,0) and every consecutive pair differs by {|dr|,|dc|} = {1,2}.

a.n: Approach 1: Invert and verify consecutive moves
a.i: Bucket cells by their visit number, then check each adjacent pair of steps for a knight move. No DFS/BFS needed since the order is fully specified.
s: Fill pos[t] = (row, col) for each cell.
For t = 1..n²−1 check |dr|,|dc| is {1,2}; fail otherwise.
a.t: O(n²) — one pass to invert the grid, one pass to verify moves

w: The main pitfall is missing the grid[0][0] == 0 check — a tour starting elsewhere is invalid even if all moves look legal. Some solutions instead walk forward from (0,0) looking up where step t+1 sits; equivalent cost. Follow-up: count the number of valid knight tours (backtracking with Warnsdorff heuristic), or verify tours on non-square boards.
